# Product Research And Validation

Apply these checkpoints when defining the product direction for the platform.

## Core Focus

- Keep the main audience explicit: identify the first coach segments to serve, such as life, business, fitness, or other niches.
- Prioritize direct conversations with 5-10 coaches to understand their current sales flow, pain points, and tool stack.
- Evaluate competitors across no-code products, prompt tools, and coach-oriented platforms.
- Clarify the main differentiator versus tools like Notion, Gumroad, and Zapier.
- Limit initial scope to 3-5 concrete use cases, such as PDF access, mini-course delivery, Q&A bot, or funnel support.
- Choose a pricing model deliberately: per coach, per workspace, per seat, or per usage.
- Validate the concept quickly with 2-3 coaches, including willingness to pay.

## Checklist

- [ ] Define the primary coach persona and early adopter profile.
- [ ] Run and document 5-10 coach interviews.
- [ ] Summarize the current workflow coaches use to sell and deliver value.
- [ ] Map the main competitors, substitutes, and gaps in the market.
- [ ] Write a clear core value statement for the product.
- [ ] Select the first 3-5 use cases to support.
- [ ] Decide the initial pricing model and rationale.
- [ ] Validate desirability and price sensitivity with 2-3 real coaches.

## Output Expectations

- Produce concrete decisions, not generic brainstorming.
- Prefer short decision docs with explicit tradeoffs and open questions.
- When assumptions are unverified, flag them and convert them into research tasks.
